This week on the anvil, in light of a lot of apparent disagreement going around on the subject: genetically modified food products ("GMOs"). For those who haven't seen these posts before, this is part of a recurring series of open-ended discussion posts designed to foster more detailed debate rather than reactions to news stories or articles. I believe that the best way to arrive at the ideal conclusion in many things is to forge one's opinions on the anvil of debate, hence the title. So, let's talk GMOs. Some suggested questions to think about:

  • What is a GMO (i.e. does the term include selective breeding or only modern techniques)?

  • Do GMOs have effects on human health if eaten?

  • Should there be any legal restrictions on the creation/use of GMOs (e.g. mandatory labeling)?

As always, in the interests of a neutral discussion I will wait to discuss my own opinions until others have had a good chance to do so.
RE: "e.g. mandatory labeling"; How have European countries handled the issue and why did they handle it that way?

They seem to have taken various approaches. The EU subjects all GMOs to rigorous testing before approving any of them, thus taking a "guilty until proven innocent" approach. So far it appears that only a very small number of GMO food products have been approved under this system, with almost all approved GMOs being for non-food purposes. Several individual European countries have banned some GMOs, and Bulgaria has banned them all outright.

Hi everyone!

I am beginning game development in unity with the purpose of getting deeply into VR interface designing and game design. I know that Mobile VR and desktop VR are pretty different so I wanted to ask you all for your opinions.

Mobile VR will be the medium to take VR into the public at-large. The mobile industry is growing tremendously and is much more widespread than powerful desktop computers around the world. But the quality at the moment, compared between the two, favors desktop VR.

I want to enter the VR world at my best by impacting the most people possible. So I think Mobile VR is the route I'd like to go. Are there any huge drawbacks in hanging out purely in Mobile? What do your workflows look like? Do you make desktop VR apps and then 'downscale' them into mobile experiences?
New developer - planning for the future

Hey there. Sounds like you are on the right path. I think mobile will surely take over the desktop arena. So I would focus a bit on mobile, but frankly the medium is so new there are no guarantees yet.

At this point I would worry less about mobile vers desktop and just get to working in VR. There is lots to learn and lots to discover yet. There are no locked in workflows yet. the tools are changing weekly, the delivery is changing monthly. New ideas are popping up and then floundering to be replaced with newer ideas. Unity is good tool as you can downscale to mobile from a full featured.

and your doing it right. those that jump on board now will be industry leaders in 18 months regardless of platform. The concepts and ideas you generate now, will be come best practices for those in the future. Welcome to the bleeding edge! ;-) program.
